sections.title: Indoor Storage of Combustible Liquids
sections.text: The maximum allowable quantity of Class II combustible liquids stored inside a building shall not exceed 660 gallons per control area at the floor level. Quantities exceeding this limit require the area to be classified as a Group H-3 occupancy.

sections.title: H-3 Occupancy Requirements
sections.text: Areas classified as H-3 shall be separated from other occupancies by fire barriers having a fire-resistance rating of not less than 2 hours. Explosion venting shall be provided in accordance with Section 911.

sections.title: Group A (Assembly) Fire Alarm
sections.text: A manual fire alarm system that activates the occupant notification system shall be installed in Group A occupancies having an occupant load of 300 or more.

sections.title: Group I (Institutional) Fire Alarm
sections.text: A manual fire alarm system shall be installed in Group I occupancies. An automatic smoke detection system shall be installed in corridors, waiting areas, and habitable spaces in Group I-2 occupancies.

sections.title: Automatic Sprinkler Systems - Group A
sections.text: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided for Group A-1 occupancies where the fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet, the fire area has an occupant load of 300 or more, or the fire area is located on a floor other than a level of exit discharge.

sections.title: Generator Fuel Tanks
sections.text: Fuel tanks for emergency and standby power generators shall comply with Section 5704.2 for above-ground tanks. Sub-base tanks shall be UL 142 listed and provided with secondary containment and leak detection.

sections.title: Maximum Allowable Quantity Per Control Area - Storage
sections.text: Class II Combustible Liquid: 660 gallons (floor level), 330 gallons (above floor level). Class IIIA Combustible Liquid: 1,375 gallons (floor level). Class IIIB Combustible Liquid: 13,200 gallons (floor level).

sections.title: Standards for Fire Protection Systems
sections.text: Fire protection systems shall be maintained in accordance with the applicable referenced standard. Systems shall be tested and inspected per NFPA 25 (sprinklers), NFPA 72 (fire alarm), and NFPA 13 (installation).

sections.title: Emergency Escape and Rescue Openings
sections.text: Basements and sleeping rooms below the fourth story shall have at least one exterior emergency escape and rescue opening. The opening shall have a minimum net clear opening of 5.7 square feet (5.0 SF at grade floor).

sections.title: Fire Command Center
sections.text: A fire command center shall be provided in buildings that are more than 75 feet in height. The fire command center shall be a minimum of 200 square feet with a minimum dimension of 10 feet.
